44334.text: This wavekin secretes a coat of oily mucus that allows it to adapt to subtle changes in water temperature, and is prized by artisans for its utility in the production of heavy-duty lubricants.
44334.name: Oily Ropefish

44335.text: Found in the depths of Yak Awak Tsoly, these twinkling spheroid creatures are a valuable (if somewhat dim) light source for the people of the Ut'ohmu Horizon.
44335.name: Yak Awak Core

44336.text: Like many octopodes, this wavekin hides in a cloud of its own ink when threatened. After sailors noticed that this particular ink left a nearly permanent stain upon everything it touched, it was soon adopted for use in nautical mapmaking.
44336.name: Inktopus

44337.text: This aquatic invertebrate was named for the hexagonal pores in its spongin mesh. Once its living cells have been cruelly stripped away, its skeletal remains can be used to create luxurious lathers with the soap of one's choice.
44337.name: Honeycomb Sponge

44338.text: The thick shell of this wavekin, found only in saltwater cenotes, is pulverized and added to soil to improve its drainage. Historically, this has saved countless structures from damage during heavy rain.
44338.name: Cenote Oyster

47988.text: Compared to its timid lesser brethren, this wavekin is bestowed with a positively brazen temperament, and is often spotted leading shoals around the shallows near the For'ard Cabins with a self-assured grace. Guests have likened its presence to that of a conscientious, well-versed caretaker.
47988.name: Cabinkeep Permit

47989.text: As pleated matamata age, their shells continue to grow indefinitely. According to legend, the largest and most ancient specimens eventually fuse with the landscape, blocking rivers in the process─the once-mighty roar of water reduced to a mere muttering. Though naturalists have yet to observe the phenomena in the wild, this specimen renders the tales believable.
47989.name: Muttering Matamata

47990.text: Capable of singlehandedly reducing the largest of predators to naught but a pile of polished bones, this wavekin combines the voraciousness of its kin with an independent tenacity that is chilling to behold.
47990.name: Riverlong Candiru

47991.text: The rhomboid form of this pale yellow fish closely resembles fallen foliage. Indeed, local folklore tells of leaves borne on the wind morphing into wavekin after alighting on the surface of the Iq Br'aax reservoir.
47991.name: Deep Canopy

47992.text: Despite being considerably larger than other apoda, this ancient amphibian's chief form of defense remains the same: secreting a highly toxic slime. Unlike its smaller cousins, however, it produces toxins in such quantities as to blight the waters of the tsoly it calls home.
47992.name: Awaksbane Apoda

47993.text: The dense black roe laid by this wavekin sink down to the substrate where it spends much of its time. Known in the Hhetsarro tongue as the “swallower of dawn,” to witness this wavekin's gaping maw loom up from the depths of Lake Toari is to keenly understand the origins of its name.
47993.name: Ttokatoa

47994.text: When the scales of this flat fish catch the light, they appear to coruscate with electrical energy. This startling effect is all the more pronounced when lightning strikes nearby.
47994.name: Thunderous Flounder

47995.text: Routinely observed leading retinues of harlequin lancers with magnanimous poise, this regal wavekin lashes out with its venomous barbels to fell prey with deadly precision.
47995.name: Harlequin Queen

46188.text: Struck daily by the lightning that pours into the crackling canyons, this eel is valued for its delicate-yet-flavorful flesh that notably numbs the tongue with an electrifying spiciness.
46188.name: Goldentail

46249.text: It is believed that in the basin's pristine depths, the currents churned by Ku'uxage's falls transform themselves into aether-rich wavekin. Thus does the purple palate surely share the refined tastes of its Ku'uxage parent-waters' grand “tongue.”
46249.name: Purple Palate

46779.text: This carefree ray lives happily amongst the clouds, guided only by the wind and its own sense of adventure. Not even capture can unsettle its insouciance, as it tends to bond with the fisher that reels it in.
46779.name: Sunray Ray

46189.text: With a lifespan that exceeds even that of Yok Huy, this enormous wavekin commands the depths of Karvarhur the First while robed in thick swaths of lichen that bespeak its ancient legacy.
46189.name: Prime Adjudicator

46190.text: This large specimen of crenicichla dominates the shoreline waters of Miyakabek'zoma, boasting the elegant and unmarred fins of an absolute victor.
46190.name: Crenicichla Miyaka

46191.text: While the skins of related species can be processed into armor, the sable scales of this primordial wavekin boast even greater toughness, and are sturdy enough to substitute as weaponry without alteration.
46191.name: Iron Shadowtongue

46192.text: Said to spring forth from sunbeams as radiant droplets, these wavekin are worth their weight in gold, for they have long been considered the ideal gift to ingratiate oneself with those in high places.
46192.name: Lotl-in-waiting

46193.text: This acrobatic wavekin is often seen leaping skyward before plummeting straight and true into the mists it calls home. On one occasion, a particularly dextrous specimen found itself the target of a mysterious traveler's probing spear tip. Predicting a swift skewering, onlookers were instead treated to a dazzling aerial display as the creature nimbly evaded defeat.
46193.name: Azure Diver

46194.text: On closer inspection, the speckled markings that adorn this wavekin are actually bud-like protrusions. Any fish lured close by the apparition of a sprouting buffet usually find themselves on the menu instead.
46194.name: Sprouting Perch

46195.text: Boasting a cavernous set of lungs proportionate to their gargantuan size, these fish have been recorded subsisting on a single lungful of air before breaching the surface again. It is difficult to assess which is more impressive─the wavekin's physical attributes, or the patience of the naturalists who waited for days on end to make such an observation.
46195.name: Gigagiant Snakehead

46196.text: This saltwater fish can be found languidly roaming the waterways of Canal Town, shoals of lesser wavekin in tow. To exert control over its territory, it plies the same routes back and forth with the consistency of a commercial ferry service.
46196.name: Gondola Louvar

49794.text: Clad in glinting golden scales, these substantial wavekin resemble pouches laden with coin. Those fooled by the illusion often dive into the water after glimpsing the fish, visions of wealth soon vanishing with the creature's retreating form.
49794.name: Purse of Riches

49795.text: Although known to primarily target hapless peddlers and other waterside wanderers, with increased punutiy traffic in the region, these voracious carnivores now enjoy a more varied diet─much to the chagrin of the punutiy handlers and their gentle charges.
49795.name: Punutiy Pain

49796.text: Some scholars have likened this wavekin's form to an ear of corn. Indeed, the sight of these fish basking in the sun with their silk-like tailfins aquiver is akin to that of a golden field, ripe kernels ready to harvest.
49796.name: Shuckfin Dace

49797.text: A species of flat catfish residing in the shallow waters of Ankledeep. Locals wading in are often met with the tickling touch of barbels as the pool's residents greet their shins with cautious interest.
49797.name: Shin Snuffler

49798.text: Presiding over Cenote Moxutural with an apparent sense of ownership, this mighty gar once frolicked with local residents. Since the nearby village fell silent, however, it has kept a lonesome vigil in the depths.
49798.name: Moxutural Greatgar

49799.text: This golden wavekin is found in the deepest recesses beyond the submerged skyline. Infused with lightning energy, it wreaths itself in scraps of metal, darting through the water in a flash of scale and steel.
49799.name: Heirloom Goldgrouper

49800.text: In certain lights, this striped predator appears iridescent, its coloration shifting and shimmering as if stirred by the wind.
49800.name: Datnioides Aeroplanos

49801.text: These large and lively specimens are descended from the wavekin that once dwelled in Alexandria's castle moat. Eager to see the population flourish, naturalists chose to enshrine their hope in the naming of the fish.
49801.name: Esperance Carp

51999.text: Though the name may suggest to Eorzean speakers some association with the leftward direction, rest assured that, unlike its smaller kin, this specimen can only swim toward its right fin. Its appellation instead refers to a chant beloved by fans of a local ball-based sport─who must resist the temptation to send it soaring aloft.
51999.name: Ole Ole Ole

52000.text: Much like its lesser brethren, this formidable fish has a long history of being brandished as a blunt instrument. In the days of Yok Huy conquest, warriors encountering these wavekin in Kozama'uka would snatch the creatures from the shallows, thereby acquiring slippery─and presumably perturbed─cudgels with which to wage war.
52000.name: Iron Oxydoras

52001.text: This large freshwater fish uses its tapered, shovel-like snout to probe the riverbed, hunting for tasty morsels amidst the mud.
52001.name: Excavator Catfish

52002.text: The flat forms of these wavekin are held to wax and wane in perfect harmony with the moon. In the depths of the Ja Tiika Heartland, where the night sky is shrouded by unbroken canopy, people have long used these creatures as a kind of living calendar.
52002.name: Moonmarking Saucer

52003.text: Revered for their role in maintaining the cleanliness of water sources, these slender wavekin are considered symbols of good fortune in Mamook. Such is the reverence for these fortuitous fish that they are traditionally served at the weaning ceremonies of two-headed Mamool Ja infants.
52003.name: Autarch's Supper

52004.text: These hulking scalekin spend much of their lives in murky brackish waters, flesh slowly steeping in salt. So delicious a prize are these pre-seasoned creatures, hunters will gladly risk life and limb to bring one down.
52004.name: Bitterbark Caiman

52005.text: Appearing out of nowhere, borne on sudden, ever-shifting air currents, these tunicates are widely feared as spectral messengers from the dark depths of Zorgor─not to mention their penchant for grabbing the ankles of unwary passersby.
52005.name: Vagrant Keeper

52006.text: This gargantuan shark gleams with the brilliance of burnished copper. Some believe this luster results from a diet rich in Endless and their aether.
52006.name: Shined Copper Shark

51209.text: Owing to its green-tinged carapace and digit-like shape, Roegadyn sailors who spot one of these creatures floundering on deck will invariably ask their fellow countrymen if anyone is missing a finger. That the joke endures is less a testament to its hilarity, and more an indication that encounters with the crustacean remain a rare novelty.
51209.name: First Mate's Finger

51210.text: Many sailors consider these fish to be an ill omen, likening their pallid, shimmering forms to the souls of those lost at sea. Such superstition is easily derided─until one witnesses the chilling sight of these nigh ethereal creatures undulating beneath the waves.
51210.name: Specterfish

51211.text: One of the many permit species that thrive in waters from Eorzea to Tural. This particular variety is notably itinerant, and is known for migrating in accordance with seasonal currents.
51211.name: Rhotano Permit

51229.text: Often mistaken for common shrimp, these red-shelled crustaceans can make deft use of their scythe-like front legs.
51229.name: Red Mantis

51230.text: In the old tongue of Thavnair, this handsome crab's name means “sweet rose.” Although naturally poisonous, a judicious boiling will neutralize the toxins, providing for a safe, delectable feast.
51230.name: Datli Gwl

51231.text: Said to have started life as a fallen strand of Saint Agama's hair, the dried forms of these wavekin are often seen adorning worshipers' garments like parched little talismans.
51231.name: Agama's Strand

51212.text: This stinging anemone inhabits the shallows of the Rhotano Sea. Its barbed feelers are laced with a potent toxin that fells prey in an instant and, for some obscure reason that naturalists still struggle to ascertain, tints them a deep green.
51212.name: Rhotano Dahlia

51213.text: This specimen's name derives from its slender, cylindrical form, as well as several recorded instances of lodesmen losing their quills overboard and resorting to questionable measures to replace them. One has to pity the luckless wavekin hauled from the depths and subjected to multiple snout-first inkwell dippings.
51213.name: Lodesmate's Pen

51214.text: This exceptionally aggressive wavekin is a common sight in the waters betwixt Thavnair and Eorzea. Some jokingly remark that its temperament must be learned from the pirates who ply their cutthroat trade in the region.
51214.name: Rhotano Roosterfish

51232.text: The steely glint of this wavekin's dorsal fins evokes the weapons wielded by Thavnair's temple guardians. Perhaps it too watches over some sacred site in the depths.
51232.name: Palaka's Blade

51233.text: Long seen as harbingers of inclement weather, this wavekin's name approximates to “rain cloud” in the common tongue. While these fish do indeed tend to appear before storms hit, naturalists posit they are simply fleeing as fast as their little fins will carry them.
51233.name: Parjanya Wrasse

51234.text: Though this leviathan is equipped with noteworthy jaws capable of shredding prey to pieces, this scalekin's name actually means “blunt-nosed thief.” Presumably this is a reference to it snatching the lives of any creatures foolish enough to contest its reign in the depths.
51234.name: Simolestes

51215.text: Unlike its mosasaur cousins that stalk the waters of inland Gyr Abania, this scalekin freely roams the realm's oceans. Despite presiding over a much larger habitat, its innate ferocity remains unchanged.
51215.name: Rhotanosaurus

51216.text: Legend has it that an envoy's attendant fell from their vessel while traversing the seas, whereupon they assumed a new, aquatic form beneath the waves─kimono transforming into scale, stitch by vibrant stitch.
51216.name: Royal Handmaiden

51235.text: This ancient reptile inhabits the seas near Thavnair, where it enjoys enduring favor amongst the populace, appearing in folklore and myriad local tales. For despite its glistening maw of razor-sharp teeth, the Thavnasaurus has a remarkably gentle temperament.
51235.name: Thavnasaurus

51687.text: The calmest, most carefree inhabitant of Thavnairian coastal waters, this wavekin bears the markings of its approximate Hingan namesake: a breezy patterned garment traditionally worn during the warm summer months.
51687.name: Junior Jinbei

51218.text: When these vibrantly striped wavekin were first spotted frolicking offshore by a group of island mammets, they bequeathed it with an intuitive─if not particularly inventive─name.
51218.name: Frolicsome Fish

51238.text: This subspecies is revered as a sign of good fortune in fishing villages across Thavnair. Its boldly patterned flanks are easily visible from above the water's surface, and sightings are said to precipitate a bumper catch for the day.
51238.name: Silkfin

51219.text: Of several species said to resemble a Roegadyn's formidable digits, these specimens are unquestionably the girthiest. Apparently, the creature's appellation is much to the chagrin of delicate-fingered nautical officers across the realm.
51219.name: Captain's Finger

51220.text: This colony's brilliant red coloration stems from exposure to spectral currents, and sets it apart from other more muted coral species native to La Noscea. Equally brilliant is the price it commands at market stalls─though shoppers seeking trinkets might say “eye-watering” instead.
51220.name: Bright Red Coral

51221.text: Tales speak of a royal attendant who plunged from their ship, only to transform into a resplendent wavekin in the inky depths. Some say they now ply the spectral currents with grace and determination, hoping to be reunited with their beloved former lord.
51221.name: Royal Favorite

51222.text: Long associated with wealth and fortune, many believe this wavekin's raiment of gold-rimmed scales resembles a clutch of hoarded treasure.
51222.name: Pirate's Purse

51223.text: Belonging to a species of wavekin that have the occasional misfortune of being used as writing implements, these specimens are noted for their impressive size. Presumably their indignation when being brandished as a pen is all the greater for this.
51223.name: Captain's Pen

51224.text: Deriving from its protruding cylindrical snout, this ancient scalekin's name roughly translates to “knobbed lizard.” Some specimens grow to such a colossal size that they are mistaken for whales.
51224.name: Tylosaurus

51225.text: This wide-roaming wavekin is frequently sighted riding spectral currents near the Cieldalaes, fluttering its spiny fins as if dancing to some distant rhythm.
51225.name: Cieldalaes Roosterfish

51226.text: This vicious monstrosity descends upon the spectral currents like a dread shadow, unassailable dominance secured with brutal strength and deadly fangs.
51226.name: Renegade Rhotanosaurus

51227.text: This wavekin's red, seedlike form conjures thoughts of abundance and plenty. For this reason, it is prized as a symbol of good fortune among spearfishers and divers alike.
51227.name: Red Boarfish

51239.text: This variety of red mantis displays even more exuberant coloration than its cousins. Though this vivid hue dulls to an ash grey after cooking, the flesh remains simply scrumptious with a pinch of salt.
51239.name: Great Red Mantis

51240.text: Exposure to spectral currents seems to have further heightened this crustacean's already exceptional beauty─and taste. This pedigree is unambiguously reflected in its name: “resplendent rose,” as well as the fact it is routinely served at the satrap's palace.
51240.name: Guzel Gwl

51241.text: The distinct pattern adorning the scales of this flat fish resembles the glinting eye of some deep-sea behemoth. Indeed, the illusion is enough to send even wavekin much larger than darpana fleeing in terror.
51241.name: Darpana

51242.text: When dried, these slender, sharp-nosed fish make for excellent projectiles. Some Thavnairian merchants have even taken to launching them at wall-mounted maps, planning their next excursion based on where the silver snout pierces the parchment. One wonders how many businesses have floundered as the result of an errant throw.
51242.name: Silverdart

51243.text: Over the millennia, this ancient species has been much transformed by its time spent traversing spectral currents. In recent years, this specimen has garnered significant attention among Sharlayan scholars devoted to the study of underwater aetheric currents.
51243.name: Satrapsaurus

51244.text: Although large for mantis shrimp, these tiger-striped crustaceans are extremely timid. They spend much of their time cowering on the seabed, rarely moving unless swept up in a spectral current.
51244.name: Tiger Mantis

51245.text: This mahi-mahi subspecies moves at an infuriatingly ponderous pace. Seeking sport, some Thavnairian fishers will attempt to harry the creature along, though seldom to any avail. Apparently, even the sight of a fishing boat's prow bearing down upon it isn't enough to rouse a mehi-mahi from its leisurely locomotion.
51245.name: Mehi-mahi

51246.text: This venerable scalekin is endowed with rows of saw-like teeth, which it uses to terrifying effect in dispatching hapless prey. Mere mention of its name─and the image of those dreadful fangs that inevitably follows─is enough to strike fear into the hearts of veteran fishers, and shred any confidence that mere ilms of timber might keep one safe from harm.
51246.name: Pliosaurus

51217.text: Prolonged exposure to high concentrations of aether has partially crystallized these curious wavekin. They are frequently sighted at the forefront of spectral currents, calling to mind stars streaking across the firmament.
51217.name: Spectral Starfish

51237.text: The semi-crystalline flesh of this grouper results from absorbing a surfeit of aether over its lifespan─most of which it spends swimming at the vanguard of spectral currents.
51237.name: Spectral Grouper

51228.text: These sizable turtles traverse the seas with their shells held above the waves. Thus exposed to the elements, their carapaces become a rich tapestry of plant life, with the oldest specimens playing host to unique, highly complex ecosystems.
51228.name: Akupara

51247.text: With an imposing name befitting a serpent possessing such massive saber-like tusks, Manasvin is heralded in the Near East as a warder of evil spirits─who are presumably as fearful of being skewered as any mortal would be.
51247.name: Manasvin

52012.text: Named an “envoy of rainbows” in the Hanuhanu tongue, this fish gleams in seven distinct colors. Its scales are as popular as precious stones when it comes to decoration due to their brilliance and luster.
52012.name: Pote'uka

52013.text: Blooms of these jellyfish can be found off the docks of High Tide Harbor. When dried, their durability and elasticity make them valued packaging amongst traders.
52013.name: Harbor Cloud

52014.text: Exceedingly agile, this shrimp bears a name evocative of rust and deadly shears. Its tight ruddy-brown carapace conceals flesh bountiful in nourishment.
52014.name: Iq Ebaji

52015.text: Squid native to the waters beneath Zorgor the Boundless. While the Tonawawta have used its ink as pigment since days of eld, its flesh is considered inedible by even the most ambitious epicureans.
52015.name: Yowekwa Inkhead

52016.text: This remarkable species breathes by means of lungs, perhaps due to the shoals where it resides. Exhalations are summarily absorbed by the body, which creates enough carbonic acid to trigger a popping noise upon exposure to air.
52016.name: Burst Lungfish

52007.text: This wavekin's vibrant flanks call to mind the iridescent strata of Worqor Lar Dor. Indeed, legend has it that the creature began life as a chunk of rock from that mighty edifice that plunged into a lake after being seized by sudden thirst.
52007.name: Ner Lar Dor

52008.text: Rimed with algae and wreathed in foliage, this still, silent hunter lurks in the gloomy substrate of Miyakabek'zu. Intriguingly, the crystalline protrusions on its back share the same internal structure as many precious gems.
52008.name: Xehabopo'u

52009.text: While Eorzean eyes might associate this wavekin's rounded form with that of a heart, for the Mamool Ja, this revered creature is a symbol of the sky itself─a facet of the firmament glimpsed briefly through the swaying canopy above.
52009.name: Skyfrond

52010.text: Some naturalists believe─against all evidence to the contrary─that rroneek are in fact a species of fish, and point to this ancient horned wavekin as some kind of progenitor. Regardless of one's thoughts on the matter, the creature's horns certainly evoke their land-dwelling namesake.
52010.name: Rroneek Bichir

52297.text: Formed when lesser balls of lightning collide and fuse, these colossal, coruscating specimens are exceptionally volatile. The slightest rupture in its outer membrane can result in a catastrophic discharge of levin─a phenomenon which has left more than one curious naturalist frazzled...or worse.
52297.name: Great Ball of Lightning

52011.text: Endowed with three curving, scythe-like fins, this terrifying wavekin is the culmination of experiments to replicate an ancient sea monster. When its creators discovered it could cleave through electrope with unsettling ease, they began to regret their success.
52011.name: Triple Threat

20144.text: Those who dare gaze into its swirling whorls risk spiraling into infinite madness. Luckily, few have peered into that void, as an intact specimen of this fragile shell is scarcely to be found.
20144.name: Wentletrap

20145.text: Despite its name, the shading of this protogynous species is subject to variation as it transitions genders. As a result, some infer that its tenebrous title in fact references the deadly, viscous toxin it secretes.
20145.name: Black Boxfish

20146.text: The glass manta is known as a languorous, lackadaisical wayfarer whose striped ray brethren were domesticated by the Kojin long ago.
20146.name: Glass Manta

20147.text: Originally brought over as tribute to the bakufu of Hingashi by an emissary from Radz–at–Han, the diplomat himself could not have taken to his new habitat as well as these fish have.
20147.name: Regal Silverside

20148.text: This moray maintains a symbiotic relationship with the spiny lobster, providing protection to the crustacean while the lobster lures forth the octopodes on which the wavekin feeds.
20148.name: Snowflake Moray

20149.text: A well-known children's story in Doma tells of a complacent hoppfish given to pondering the unbearable lightness of being, an allegory of existential thought positing that each has but one life to fish.
20149.name: Hoppfish

20150.text: Wrapped in a tough, scaly cuirass and always craving the crunch of bones and shells, this hardest of links in the food chain has a name synonymous with grit in Doman vernacular.
20150.name: Lightscale

20151.text: Per the axiom “the harder the battle, the sweeter the victory,” this notoriously difficult-to-land blowfish is as much loathed by fishermen as it is loved by diners.
20151.name: Grass Fugu

20152.text: What it loses to the Doman eel in terms of flavor, the giant eel more than makes up with in volume, and those who value a full belly will certainly get their gil's worth out of this oversized creature.
20152.name: Giant Eel

20153.text: This hermit crab spins its way through several spiral shells over the course of its curmudgeonly life, gradually grabbing larger domiciles as it chases pesky neighbors away from its property.
20153.name: Kamina Crab

20154.text: Based on history, we know this massive crab can extend its major claws to span the width of two adult Hyurs set shoulder to shoulder.
20154.name: Spider Crab

20155.text: Once brought to the brink of extinction by a Thavnairian fad that claimed these fish could unlock the secret to eternal youth, the species was saved at the last moment by a shift in popular attitudes toward growing old gracefully.
20155.name: Little Dragonfish

20156.text: The precise purpose of its dual dorsal fins remains a mystery to scholars, as observing the dark fish in its native deep-sea environs has proven nigh impossible.
20156.name: Black Fanfish

20157.text: The vertical black-and-white striping that identifies these sharks disappears as the pups mature, and for a long time, youth and adult specimens were considered altogether separate species.
20157.name: Zebra Shark

20158.text: With a morose, bony appearance and purported powers to ward off evil spirits, it should come as no surprise this shell is a popular trinket with those who fly the skull and crossbones.
20158.name: Nophica's Comb

20159.text: This repulsive breed of languid swimmers' only chance of drawing near to fellow sea creatures is to dangle bait from their protrusions and hope others are not revolted.
20159.name: Warty Wartfish

20160.text: Ubiquitous and unremarkable shellfish tucked in among the rocks and algae along Othardian river- and lakebeds. These whelks are essentially what fish feed on when they can't be bothered to hunt for something better.
20160.name: Common Whelk

20161.text: It is indeed a curiosity how a herbivorous fish should chance to grow to Roegadyn dimensions in length, but the vegetarian diet at least helps explain this fish's youthful, clean-shaven appearance.
20161.name: Hairless Barb

20162.text: The bioluminescent organs that cause this slight-bodied fish to glow in the dark are sometimes mistaken by fishers for drowned spirits lost at sea from afar, but there is no mistaking the wavekin's disproportionately enormous head.
20162.name: Hatchetfish

20163.text: While this fish may not technically be inedible, its string-like fin fibers make for a meal that will under no circumstances go down smoothly, and the flesh reeks of rot to boot.
20163.name: Threadfish

20164.text: Though this eel may be named for its affinity for green, its aversion to land should assuage growers' fears of one turning up in the garden.
20164.name: Garden Eel

20165.text: Overlooked in most cultures due to its voidsent likeness, the Hingashi see past the repugnant exterior of this prize ingredient and find the hidden delectability underneath.
20165.name: Eastern Sea Pickle

20166.text: From shellfish and small fry to turtles and baby sharks, this fish has an appetite for everything, and the Kojin discipline little wrongdoers by warning them the brindlebass seeks out naughty children for supper.
20166.name: Brindlebass

20167.text: It is well-known that the spina of its fins are laced with a virulent toxin, yet still the promise of its tender, white flesh tempts many a fisher into an early grave.
20167.name: Demon Stonefish

20168.text: This offshoot of the Doman crayfish boasts a vibrant sanguine-toned plate, a stark contrast to the other members of its family.
20168.name: Armored Crayfish

20169.text: One of the four great fish of Doma, its delights were once a rare treat for the privileged, but have since been made available to the masses via farming.
20169.name: Bighead Carp

20170.text: The shells of this wavekin once served as the coin of the realm in the lands of Yanxia, to which the Hingan term “zeni” refers, though the mollusk is all but worthless nowadays.
20170.name: Zeni Clam

20171.text: The corpse-eater is a large carnivorous fish that rides the warm currents into the Ruby Sea. Its unfortunate habit of gathering around floating bodies has resulted in an undeservedly grim name. For the record, any corpses the fish may have been caught nibbling on were dead before the fish found them.
20171.name: Corpse-eater

20172.text: Its rugged facial features, scar-like stripe, and solitary swimming habits earned this fish the Hingan title of “ronin,” or “wandering warrior.” The fish does not seem to actively seek a master.
20172.name: Ronin Trevally

20173.text: To taste a toothsome grouper is to enter a higher plane of flavorful bliss; to catch one, divine.
20173.name: Toothsome Grouper

20174.text: This popular Far Eastern treat spends its evenings scouring the reef with its radula, delicately sifting through and devouring scrumptious strands of seaweed.
20174.name: Horned Turban

20175.text: In case you were wondering, correcting friends and family members who erroneously refer to this species as a “red starfish” does indeed make you a pedant.
20175.name: Ruby Sea Star

20176.text: This crab runs the migratory gauntlet of the river, starting out at the basin, then venturing upstream to freshwater in midlife before ultimately returning out to sea to bear its young.
20176.name: Gauntlet Crab

20177.text: Just your typical, average, run-of-the-mill case of a reclusive ascetic fasting to the point of infirmity, stumbling and tumbling into a river, receiving the mercy of the gods, and having his spirit transmigrated into a fish.
20177.name: Hermit Goby

20178.text: A fish of famed longevity that has swum the One River since time immemorial in search of enlightenment, with a few supposedly having ascended to the heavens above.
20178.name: Skythorn

20179.text: A squid with a reputation for getting around, this sharp cephalopod resides on plates all over the Far East. Delicious whether raw or battered.
20179.name: Swordtip

20180.text: A scad or not a scad? That is the question that confronts scholars who ponder the nomenclature of this undefinable fish, a pioneering maverick that defiantly straddles taxonomical lines and chooses to live beyond labels.
20180.name: False Scad

20181.text: Spontaneous though it may be, occasionally a species will simply be named after the first thing its finder spies in the vicinity, as in the case of this cold-climate crustacean.
20181.name: Snow Crab

20182.text: Even amid the scarce light of the deep, its highly reflective eyes shine a bright-red beacon, and its name has inspired numerous groan-worthy “how did the lates eyes get so red” punchlines among schoolchildren desperate for attention.
20182.name: Red-eyed Lates

20183.text: After the eggs are laid in autumn, the hatchlings battle winter's chill to emerge full-grown in spring, constituting an entirely common life cycle with nothing in particular to be bitter about, really.
20183.name: Common Bitterling

20184.text: Despite complete and utter inattention to diet and exercise, this longevous fish still manages to see its fair share of summers, not uncommonly more than the fishermen who pursue it.
20184.name: Fifty-summer Cod

20185.text: This wavekin's dubious origin story tells of a snake who wished to swim in the river despite the fact that snakes and fish are in no way related, though in fairness, the small up-top, long-in-the-back form of the mullet does bear a slight ophidian resemblance.
20185.name: Nagxian Mullet

20186.text: Whiling the daylight hours away under the cover of rock, this fish comes out at night to paint the sea red─two coats!
20186.name: Redcoat

20187.text: This tiny floating tiger earns its stripes by hunting plankton with catlike precision, but its gluttonous appetite threatens to turn its stripes into rings.
20187.name: Yanxian Tiger Prawn

20188.text: A holy hand fan called forth the rains that doused the fires of the mountain, only for the great butterfingered tengu to then unceremoniously drop it into the One River, whereupon it metamorphosed into this stormy electric ray. True story.
20188.name: Tengu Fan

20189.text: The trained eye will appreciate the lamellated striae and tuberculate folds of the concentric whorls atop its squamous base, its thin, arcuate columella, and lustrous operculum. The untrained eye will appreciate a pretty shell.
20189.name: Star Turban

20190.text: Most somber-toned of the four great fish of Doma. Having nourished the masses for generations, the blue-fish has swum its way into Doman folklore alongside the mythical onefish, twofish, and red-fish.
20190.name: Blue-fish

20191.text: This naughty nocturnal croaker has a habit of getting itself into hot water, namely Yanxian and Nagxian cauldrons.
20191.name: Steppe Bullfrog

20192.text: The “cavalry” of its name arrives from the popular rumor that an esurient school of the catfish split a river-fording horse in two, devouring it from the stomach out. Horse-lovers and the weak of stomach might steer clear of this “meal that eats you back.”
20192.name: Cavalry Catfish

20193.text: While more imaginative Xaela may convince themselves that this fish's eponymous appendage heralds the dawn and renders its kin to the almighty Azim, sometimes a red fin is just a red fin.
20193.name: Redfin

20194.text: Having fallen in a teardrop as the moon above wept into the sea below, this pious disc-in-water offers prayers to the Lover each full moon in hopes of returning home.
20194.name: Moondisc

20195.text: One might mistakenly assume this bonytongue was left out in the sun too long, but the pigmentation of its glistening scales actually owes more to its saline habitat.
20195.name: Bleached Bonytongue

20196.text: This merciless lord of Loch Seld rules with an iron fin, visiting a nightly reign of terror upon the indigenous flood tuna, who live in perpetual fear of the salty tyrant.
20196.name: Salt Shark

20197.text: The sky-colored shine of its tapetum evokes the proud image of Ala Mhigan regalia, but the cape is only as good as the king, and the fish was unduly subjected to symbolic slaughter following the fall of Theodoric.
20197.name: King's Mantle

20198.text: Discovery of this “new” bioluminescent species has been hailed as a breakthrough by academics, but the Kojin, who have dwelled beside the fish for countless generations, do not see what all the fuss is about.
20198.name: Sea Lamp

20199.text: Despite being the largest fish in its family, this exceptional hunter is remarkably fast, and sure to go quickly when served for supper as well.
20199.name: Amberjack

20200.text: Whether it is named for the fruit of the season in which it is oft seen or named for the sweetness of its flesh, under no circumstances should fish be paired with fruit.
20200.name: Cherry Salmon

20201.text: Borrowing its name from the Hingan word for the “flowers” of sintered sediment found in hot springs, this crab has the curious ability to warm the waters around itself, not unlike younglings in a pool.
20201.name: Yu-no-hana Crab

20202.text: The namesake gudgeon of the Nhaama desert dwellers is also a kindred spirit, abiding the daylight's arc amid the shade of rocks, and emerging to hunt only at night.
20202.name: Dotharli Gudgeon

20203.text: One man's dross is another man's dinner with these clams, and while the Xaela may turn their nose up in the steppes, the Yanxians are more than happy to chow down by the river.
20203.name: River Clam

20204.text: Fret not─this herbivorous catfish posing as a land shark is little more than a paper tiger.
20204.name: Grass Shark

20205.text: These shrimp literally rained from the heavens above Gyr Abania after being swept up in the seismic sea storms of the Calamity.
20205.name: Typhoon Shrimp

20206.text: The saviors of your dinner party come complete with their own dish. Simply soak the salt and sand out before serving to enjoy these heroes in the half shell.
20206.name: Rock Oyster

20207.text: The whitening effect of salt-absorption is favored by natural selection amid the saline climes, and the seasoning effect is favored by Highlanders, who enjoy the urchins raw.
20207.name: Salt Urchin

20208.text: An expert at meticulously crafting dwellings out of salt licks, this architectural crustacean's schematic weakness lies in its failure to build in a backdoor, allowing itself to be cornered by all too many guileful fishermen.
20208.name: Carpenter Crab

20209.text: To small sea creatures, this aquatic warrior strikes an imposing profile─clad in a chitinous, segmented exoskeleton of armor, brandishing menacing pincers, and flailing thick, whip-like antennae. Gods be praised they are tiny.
20209.name: Spiny Lobster

20210.text: While the shark bears the name of the venerated Far Eastern sea scholar who discovered it, genealogy hints that it is actually an ancestor of the Allagan bladeshark.
20210.name: Mitsukuri Shark

20211.text: Initially the unintended by-product of rabid inbreeding among market goldfish, the Doman bubble eye has stabilized into a viable species with an eye-popping following, no doubt owing to its vibrant coloring and caricaturish expressions.
20211.name: Doman Bubble Eye

20212.text: An old Doman fable tells of a presumptuous squeaker who sought to soar where only dragons dare venture, and was cast to the depths of the sea as punishment, never to surface again.
20212.name: Dragon Squeaker

20213.text: Denizen of the middle and lower rivers of Othard who loyally serves as the eyes of the Dawn Father, to hear the Xaela tell it.
20213.name: Dawn Herald

20214.text: While a few are to be found in Loch Seld, one is far more likely to come across this swirly shell atop the tables of Ala Mhigo, where the cellar's abode is routinely repurposed into a salt shaker.
20214.name: Salt Cellar

20215.text: While fishmongers may carry cuts of this sturgeon, it is the caviar, marinated to perfection in the brine of Loch Seld, that is worth its weight in gold.
20215.name: White Sturgeon

20216.text: The toothy grin this ruthless long-jawed killer flashes before bearing down on its prey will be a familiar sight to debtors who've taken loans from sharks of a different sort.
20216.name: Tithe Collector

20217.text: With winglike fins, this dark crusader glides through the sea, a hero fighting for the small fry. The bashful bat relies not on witchery, instead prevailing with its physical prowess, genius intellect, and indomitable will.
20217.name: Bashful Batfish

20218.text: From the brackish estuaries to the fresh waters upstream, these protandrous fish visit every ilm of the river over the course of their lives.
20218.name: River Bream

20219.text: Myriad twisted tales of drowned souls have been tied to the eerie, rope-like appearance of this otherwise harmless anguilliform fish, whose only crime is wanting a hug.
20219.name: Snipe Eel

20220.text: The precious shade of pink worn by this adorable little angel tempts one to pinch its heavenly little fish cheeks. These domesticated darlings can be found watching over many an aquatic garden.
20220.name: Cherubfish

20221.text: Looming larger than her dawn relative, the dusk herald benights the waters with silver-blue scales of twilight in devout service to Nhaama.
20221.name: Dusk Herald

20222.text: Fiercely territorial from birth, the younglings seek to intimidate any and all who enter their perceived sphere of dominion, kin included; a posture that sits perfectly well with the Oronir.
20222.name: Glaring Perch

20223.text: This pipira's saltwater habitat seasons it to perfection, soliciting no assistance on the part of the cook other than to slap the fish on the grill, making for an unmistakable taste of Ala Mhigo the first time, and every time.
20223.name: Abalathian Pipira

20224.text: Before reaching out to caress the smooth and lustrous chrome of this seemingly metallic specimen, be forewarned that it is indeed a slimy, smelly fish.
20224.name: Steel Loach

20225.text: While the sole may resemble the bottom of a foot, this fastidious fish is mindful not to tread on its predators' toes, and its ivory sheen allows it to step lightly among the flora of the lake floor.
20225.name: Ivory Sole

20226.text: A slough of unflattering sobriquets, many of which cannot be uttered in polite company, are ascribed to this beakfish at its various phases of development, hence its “motley” moniker. Needless to say, the tale of the ugly beakfish does not end happily.
20226.name: Motley Beakfish

20227.text: When one predatory trait far exceeds any local resistance, a species is wont to remain largely the same, and such is the case of this immutable scalekin, whose preternatural olfactory sense has allowed it to sniff out prey, track the scent, and stave off adaptation for ages.
20227.name: Thousandfang

20228.text: Researchers spent decades attempting to mark the spot where this scalekin fell on the ancestral scale between fish and dolphin only to recently find that it had never actually gone extinct.
20228.name: Ichthyosaur

20229.text: The braggadocio of the sailfin landed it in the One River, as the mighty Susano put the arrogant fish in its place by casting it out of the Ruby Sea, banishing it from its home for once and for all.
20229.name: Sailfin

20230.text: Possessed of an imposing frame and whiskers that speak to its wisdom, this fish calls to mind the balance of body and spirit embodied by the ancient masters, and appears cognizant of nature's innermost secrets.
20230.name: Fangshi

20231.text: The act of swallowing the sun burned a permanent orange hue in to the scales of this hungry fire-eater and brought about the first eclipse, in case there was any question concerning how that astronomical phenomenon occurred.
20231.name: Flamefish

20232.text: Feared and reviled by the public for the role its deadly venom played in the infamous assassination of a feudal lord, the snake itself is blameless, exhibiting a passive temperament and not ordinarily given to biting.
20232.name: Fickle Krait

20233.text: Unblinking sentinel left in the wake of the Dawn Father and Dusk Mother's departure to watch over the Xaela in their absence.
20233.name: Eternal Eye

20234.text: According to the existential hierarchy of Xaela reincarnation, fishliness is next to godliness. Horses who serve their masters well in life ascend to the waters afterward, with the most noble of destriers reborn in pristine scales of white.
20234.name: Soul of the Stallion

20235.text: This fish is said to have been found atop the peaks of Abalathia's Spine following the great deluge of the Calamity, though the claims are widely regarded as wildly inaccurate, if not patently false.
20235.name: Flood Tuna

20236.text: This freelance, armed with a sturdy helm and pair of pincers, was once consulted for tactical strategy, as oracles invoked plastromancy to divine routes to victory from the lines beneath its carapace.
20236.name: Mercenary Crab

20237.text: The Sharlayans light-heartedly dubbed this fish a “butterfly,” while in Ala Mhigo it was given the macabre moniker of “wraith,” a textbook illustration of a cultural bias anecdote referenced by scholars ad infinitum despite the fact everyone has already heard it a hundred times over.
20237.name: Ashfish

20238.text: These flat, flaxen fish are instinctively drawn to floating objects, so there's a fair chance a friendly one will swim up to greet visitors in the water. Whether or not to return the hail by harpooning the fish is at the visitor's discretion.
20238.name: Silken Sunfish

20239.text: Infighting among this breed of scalekin is rampant, as merely being a member of the species atop the food chain of Loch Seld will not suffice for these bloodthirsty despots, who seek utter and total dominance over all.
20239.name: Mosasaur

20528.text: While it is the female tatsunoko who lays the eggs, it is the male who sees them through gestation in a brood pouch on its belly. And if that doesn't make you truly stop and think, nothing will.
20528.name: Tiny Tatsunoko

21179.text: Taking its name from a Hingan blade of legend, this razor-toothed wavekin is one of the few predators known to successfully hunt the slippery snailfish.
21179.name: Ichimonji

21180.text: The unusual snailfish is covered in a supple, gelatinous skin rather than scales, allowing it to wriggle free from the jaws of would-be predators.
21180.name: Snailfish

27516.text: Edible either steamed or fried, this wavekin is common throughout the waterways of Lakeland. With its ordinary appearance and undistinctive taste, the grey carp's name has become a byword for “boring.”
27516.name: Grey Carp

27517.text: This goby's large, lilac fins protect it from the attentions of hungry wildfowl. It absorbs the pigment from the purple plants that line the pools of Lakeland, making it look like a flower fallen from the very same shrubs.
27517.name: Lilac Goby

27518.text: This creature has the ability to produce a strong galvanic force, which it uses to stun prey by the schoolload. Scavengers often follow behind it to scoop up the leftovers, but if they stray too close, they too may be in for a shock.
27518.name: Purple Ghost

27520.text: Strange, twisting shadows can be seen within this sea creature's glassy skin, making them popular substitutes for crystal balls among the fortune-tellers of Lakeland. Scholars insist the visions it reveals are but the half-digested remains of its last meal.
27520.name: Gazing Glass

27522.text: This wavekin has a vicious temperament, attacking fish and fisher alike. Legend holds that these creatures are the animated spears of fallen elves who have held dominion over Lakeland since time immemorial.
27522.name: Elven Spear

27528.text: Named after its unusual ritual, wherein individuals rub their cheeks against each other, mouths opening and closing all the while. Scholars believe this aids the wavekin in establishing hierarchies of dominance within social groups.
27528.name: Skykisser

27529.text: This pretty pink and purple shellfish is a distant relative of the dusk scallop. Its flesh has the unmistakable floral flavor of viola blossoms.
27529.name: Viola Clam

27533.text: With its pure white scales representing honesty, and its peaceable demeanor representing harmony, this wavekin is often served at Lakeland wedding feasts, where the happy couple separate the sweet, steamed, fleshy flakes with a ceremonial fish knife.
27533.name: Lakeland Cod

27536.text: This fish was once a fixture on the dining tables of Voeburt, oft served stewed with a heady mix of aromatic herbs and spices. Whether this was in order to complement the fish's strong, sulphurous taste, or to mask it, is a matter for the historians.
27536.name: Big-eye

27519.text: Feeding by filtering algae and other living things from the water, this aquatic insect lacks excretory organs and uses virtually everything it eats to add to its armor. Just as well that it is an extremely light eater, or this louse would be as big as a house.
27519.name: Lakelouse

27521.text: Endemic to the Source, this cephalopod's pale purple patina helps it to remain hidden beneath the waters of Lakeland, upon whose surface is reflected the lilac-blossomed branches of the local flora.
27521.name: Source Octopus

27523.text: The gudgeon are cowardly creatures, burrowing into the lakebed to hide themselves from harm. Shade gudgeon differ only in that the high concentration of crystal in Lakeland sands stains their bodies a bright, shining white.
27523.name: Shade Gudgeon

27524.text: When the shallow pools that this wavekin lives in dry up, it crafts a cocoon from a mixture of mucus and mud, within which it hibernates. When the rains return and refill the pools, these purple pods float to the surface, looking every bit like the flowers of thistles.
27524.name: Lakethistle

27525.text: The aether this wavekin absorbs from the water makes its scales shine in a pattern peculiar to each fish. They use this to identify each other─unfortunately for them, the light they reflect also identifies them to any nearby anglers.
27525.name: Platinum Bream

27527.text: Immediately identifiable by the fat, purple body it shares with its vegetable namesake, this wavekin's appearance in the waterways around a farm heralds a bumper harvest─according to local legend, at least.
27527.name: Finned Eggplant

27530.text: This hardy fish can survive on almost any source of food and is also highly resistant to temperature changes. Where other wavekin were driven to extinction by the Flood of Light, the geayi not only survived, but thrived.
27530.name: Geayi

27531.text: Captivating in both shape and shade, the noblefish has long had pride of place in the aquariums of the high houses of Lakeland. Some say the wavekin was named after its stuck-up snout and absent chin, but this is likely naught but sour grapes.
27531.name: Noblefish

27526.text: Though its name conjures romantic images of a wizened night watchman, holding his lamp aloft as its flickering flame illuminates the path ahead, this fish's vile visage is rather more reminiscent of another kind of warden─that of an infernal gaol.
27526.name: Wardenfish

27532.text: This ancient, armored wavekin cannot see through its clouded eyes. Instead, it navigates by sensing the flow of the water against its skin, which is remarkably sensitive despite its protective plating.
27532.name: Misteye

27537.text: Princess Jenanna of the Kingdom of Voeburt weeps still for the fate of her fallen nation, her tears falling from the heavens and mingling with the waters that once belonged to her homeland.
27537.name: Jenanna's Tear

27539.text: Local legend has it that the verdant light that spilled forth from the castle of Lyhe Ghiah gave these amphibians their jadeite tint. Before the Flood, their skin was a pale pink.
27539.name: Shade Axolotl

27538.text: Named after the long spines that extend from the edges of its shell like petals, and the whorl that twists around its side like a silken scarf. Its bright-yellow color attracts curious fish, which it seizes upon with its sharp, toothy beak.
27538.name: Daisy Turban

27540.text: These small river dwellers are often offered as gifts between lovers, due to the romantic implications of the heart marks upon their heads. In captivity, it is wise to keep individuals apart, due to their unfortunate cannibalistic tendencies.
27540.name: Little Flirt

27541.text: A peallaidh is a Fuath's best friend, or so the fae folk say─and indeed, the wavekin are unusually intelligent and expressive creatures. However, when asked how they feel about the Fuath, they are wont to wear altogether more dubious faces.
27541.name: Peallaidh

27544.text: The golden fringes of this fish's fluttering fins attract the envy of every lake dweller. They have become something of a fashion accessory for the Fuath, where everyone who is anyone in polite society has one in tow.
27544.name: Gilded Batfish

27546.text: This wavekin was common throughout the waterways of Voeburt before the Flood. Its scales were once dull and grey, before the ever-playful pixies decided to give them a touch more glamour.
27546.name: Mirrorfish

27547.text: This eel's glossy, cerulean skin resembles naught more than the signature glassware of old Voeburt, leading the antique hunters of Il Mheg to christen the species the “Fool's Goblet.”
27547.name: Glass Eel

27542.text: The Voeburt bichir is easily identified by the plethora of independently agile dorsal finlets along its spine. The more a fish has, the higher its position in the dominance hierarchy, so individuals engage in vicious duels to remove their rivals' fins.
27542.name: Voeburt Bichir

27543.text: One of the many species of wavekin given a gaudy makeover by the fae folk of Il Mheg. The Fuath compete to decorate these fish, using their magicks to dress them in the most captivating patterns they can.
27543.name: Poecilia

27545.text: With its pale pink body and sky blue fins, this wavekin resembles naught more than a flower falling from a tree. It flutters its entire body from side to side as it swims, only adding to the effect.
27545.name: Petalfish

27548.text: The Voeburt salamander is a relic from the times before the Flood. It survived the crisis thanks in no small part to its incredible regenerative powers─cut off the creature's tail, and it will regrow in a matter of moons. Alas, this oft makes them the target for mischievous pixies.
27548.name: Voeburt Salamander

27549.text: During the spawning season, bedskippers have a tendency to leap about upon the surface of the water, the fluttering of their large, colorful dorsal fins looking like a storm of summer blossoms blowing across a lake.
27549.name: Bedskipper

27550.text: The dandyfish attaches great importance to its opulent appearance. Be sure to don dull clothing before entering this wavekin's waters, for it will attack anything that attracts more attention than itself on sight, and not cease until their togs are in tatters.
27550.name: Dandyfish

27552.text: Some say this strange, barely sentient creature is the result of the wandering soul of a fallen faerie taking up residence in an algal bloom, and failing to reshape its new body into its former form.
27552.name: Mock Pixie

27553.text: With its arrow-like head and sleek, shaft-like body, this scalekin flies through the water like a dart loosed from a bow. Once it has set upon a course it refuses to change direction, leading to innumerable painful prangs with underwater cliff faces.
27553.name: Hunter's Arrow

27554.text: Rulers of the lakes within which they reside due to their prodigious size, this aptly named wavekin has a habit of swallowing the frog-like fae folk whole. Luckily for the Fuath, the gobblers are unable to digest such sizable prey, and spit their victims out soon after.
27554.name: Fuathgobbler

27555.text: A wanderer who once strayed into a land of eternal springtime tells of how he met with a man who lived in a mushroom house who grew mushrooms to feed his family, who were also made of mushrooms. The moral of the story is─don't eat fungus from a crab's back.
27555.name: Paradise Crab

27556.text: An anemone that makes its home at the foot of the cliff where Saint Fathric performed his ablutionary rites. Its mane of blond tendrils resembles the hair of the short-tempered penitent, who was prone to fly into a furious rage when disturbed.
27556.name: Saint Fathric's Ire

27557.text: The jade frills of this fish's fins remind one of the ball gowns beloved by the royal ladies of Voeburt. Smaller wavekin are wont to follow in their wake in search of scraps, resembling the train of sycophants who would often attend such lofty personages.
27557.name: Queensgown

27568.text: Native to the waterways of the Rak'tika Greatwood, this small, stone-colored crab will hide itself among the riverbed rubble, attacking the ankles of any passing animals with its viselike pincers.
27568.name: Ankle Snipper

27569.text: These freshwater shellfish attach themselves to the roots of lakeside trees, looking to all the world like nothing more than another knot, thanks to their brown, bark-like patina. Eagle-eyed oyster hunters are in for a delicious, earthy treat.
27569.name: Treescale

27570.text: Depicted in Ronkan murals with brightly patterned scales, it would seem that this wavekin has faded faster over the passing of the generations than the pigments used in the ancient empire's paint.
27570.name: Ronkan Pleco

27571.text: A close cousin of the robber crab that lives alongside it, the gourmand crab is a pickier eater than its omnivorous ally, feeding only on the blue berries that lend its shell its distinctive hue.
27571.name: Gourmand Crab

27551.text: A prince from a faraway nation once gifted such a creature to Princess Sauldia of the Kingdom of Voeburt, and it has been a staple of aquariums both public and private ever since. At night, it shines with a rosy glow, signifying the ardor of her suitor's heart.
27551.name: Sauldia Ruby

27558.text: The ancestors of this bright and beautiful wavekin had scales a tawny brown, to hide themselves among the leaf litter. All that was to change when the fae folk filled Il Mheg with flowers, and the duller creatures suddenly started to stand out.
27558.name: Flowering Kelpie

27559.text: With a clear cranium revealing its innards, this weird wavekin spends most of its time buried beneath the lakebed, tubular eyes scanning the waters above. The innards of its prey also become visible when they chance to swim above it, and are torn apart by a flurry of darting teeth.
27559.name: Ghoulfish

27560.text: Known to the fae folk of Il Mheg as the “Children of the Storm,” these wavekin can deliver a stunning shock when touched. The pixies claim that they fell from the sky as lightning bolts─in truth, their skin is simply laced with a paralyzing poison.
27560.name: Measan Deala

27561.text: According to fable, a Fuath once wished to have horns on his head, and cast a spell to make it so. Alas, he neglected to specify the horns be attached, and so came to conjure this species into existence, crawling over his flustered face.
27561.name: Dohn Horn

27577.text: A larger, more aggressive cousin of the Night's bass, introduced to the Greatwood by the Night's Blessed. The wavekin's readiness to resort to violence to assert their dominion over their compeers provides a striking parallel with the Children of the Everlasting Dark.
27577.name: Everdark Bass

27562.text: Known in the world beneath the water as death incarnate, due to the ferocious manner in which they devour their prey. When a swarm of aquabloom attack a larger wavekin en masse, they resemble a great thicket, its leaves whipping to and fro in a storm.
27562.name: Aquabloom

27563.text: The jesters of ancient Voeburt would wear round, red noses and perform gymnastic tricks for the court. The swollen, scarlet eyes of this wavekin resemble the clowns' snouts, and with their ungainly swimming style, seem to be imitating their movements too.
27563.name: Jester Fish

27564.text: This freshwater fish uses its wing-shaped fins to traverse the water at alarming speeds. Some have likened it to a bolt from the blue.
27564.name: Blue Lightning

27565.text: This rather autumnal fish can look out of place in the faerie kingdom. Its eggs are a greenish yellow and give off a unique stench.
27565.name: Maidenhair

27574.text: Hermit crabs like to make homes of this mollusk's discarded shells, wearing them like a hat. In life, they migrate from place to place, feeding on the local fauna as they go. Different foodstuffs produce shells of a different color, adding another stripe each season.
27574.name: Hermit's Hood

27576.text: A carnivorous freshwater fish that looks as if it hails from a bygone age, and acts as if it has been nursing a grudge all the while. Its powerful jaws can easily tear through the scales of fish, the shells of turtles, and the armor of adventurers.
27576.name: Megapiranha

27534.text: Long has the legend of Bismarck, the great spirit of the water, been passed down among the peoples of the Source. This fish is named for the single, sharp horn it shares with its fabular brother, though its purpose is unknown─the wavekin hunts with its teeth alone.
27534.name: Little Bismarck

27567.text: Notable for its four fins that resemble a bird's wings. Only the most skilled of faerie pranksters are capable of taking on this form.
27567.name: Elder Pixie

27572.text: When the world was young, Ox'Gatorl, the keeper of the flame, taught the Ronkans how to work metal. As he tended his forge, a drop of sweat fell from his forehead and into the lake below, quenching with a hiss of steam. Thus did this copper-plated wavekin come into being.
27572.name: Gatorl's Bead

27575.text: Like a religious recluse, it lives alone in its seashell home. For reasons unknown, it refuses to take up residence in a shell of two or fewer colors, or of four or more. Only a shell striped thrice will suffice.
27575.name: Hermit Crab

27578.text: Named after a stone giant from Ronkan legend, due to its prodigious size. In ancient times, these wavekin were often offered to the imperial household as tribute─the master of the waters lying before the throne representing the emperor's dominion over all.
27578.name: Lozatl Pirarucu

27581.text: The long, flexible fins extending from this wavekin's belly allow it to steer through the water at will, describing loops and rolls with almost impertinent ease. Its movements are almost impossible to predict, resulting in many a perplexed predator.
27581.name: Rak'tika Goby

27535.text: One of an ancient order of armored fish, the bothriolepis's body is protected by thick, chitinous plates. Unlike many of its cousins it is not a skilled hunter, preferring to stir up the lakebed sand with its fins and feasting on whatever it finds.
27535.name: Bothriolepis

27566.text: Legend has it that this wavekin was once a butterfly, before being transformed into a fish by a mischievous pixie's magick. Instead of feeding on flower nectar, it nourishes itself by nibbling away at underwater weeds.
27566.name: Blue Mountain Bubble

27573.text: The shining scales of this freshwater wavekin are as hard as diamond. Suits of armor have been crafted from these scales, though they have largely been relegated to ornamental purposes due to their tendency to shatter under impact.
27573.name: Diamondtongue

27579.text: According to Ronkan legend, these large wavekin are the maidservants to the mortal form of Yx'Anpa, goddess of the harvest. Their migration patterns brought them to Ronkan lands come autumn, as if ushering in the changing of the season.
27579.name: Anpa's Handmaid

27580.text: These soft-bodied sea slugs are named for their resemblance to the long, pointed ears of the Viis. The people of Fanow reject this comparison─be sure not to speak the slug's sobriquet in the vicinity of the village, lest you find yourself on the pointy end of the rabbit ladies' lances.
27580.name: Viis Ear

36522.text: Watching their bloated, gelatinous forms drift through the waters would not whet many an appetite, but these wavekin make for a tasty treat when sufficiently dehydrated. Thus can they oft be found sun-drying on long sticks in Thavnairian fishing hamlets.
36522.name: Thavnairian Cucumber

36523.text: A crustaceous wavekin whose body is covered in razor-sharp spines to fend off potential predators, straightforwardly named by a visiting merchant from Kugane who once had the misfortune of stepping upon one.
36523.name: Spiny King Crab

36524.text: A variety of pike eel closely related to those found in the Indigo Deep. They tuck their flexible forms away in the shadowy crevices of coral reefs, launching themselves from their hidey-holes to snatch prey unawares.
36524.name: Thavnairian Eel

36525.text: These wavekin keep to reefs situated in warmer waters, where they feed off microbial organisms. The size of their dorsal and ventral fins likely correlates with their position within the hierarchy of their school.
36525.name: Gilled Topknot

36526.text: The electric organ of the Purusa fish provides not only mesmerizing illumination, but also a means by which to stun distracted prey. Its energies call to mind the invigorating spirit that flows through all living things, whence its name derives.
36526.name: Purusa Fish

36527.text: Set against the murky waters this wavekin favors, its scales' peculiar pattern makes it appear as a floating stone wall. Its sharp fangs bring to mind daggers of giantsgall, hence its vicious name.
36527.name: Giantsgall Jaw

36548.text: The thick carapaces of these wavekin resemble naught so much as a shining, sturdy coffer, which opens to reveal a sumptuous serving of delicious flesh within. Near the fishing hamlet of Onokoro, women can oft be seen diving in tireless search of these shining shellfish.
36548.name: Coffer Shell

36549.text: This grenadier's red and spiky form calls to mind Doman folklore's oni and their characteristic beards─though it admittedly most resembles a single, pitiful strand. Its oversized eyes locate smaller wavekin in a heartbeat, and its teeth make meals of them even faster.
36549.name: Onihige

36550.text: A variety of omnivorous bream with tawny scales and an undiscriminating appetite. Its taste for both bottom-dwelling shellfish and all manner of sea wrack has earned it a reputation as the sanitizer of the seafloor.
36550.name: Onokoro Carp

36551.text: As its charmingly rubescent hue and mottled carapace signal a body replete with toxins, this wavekin is better admired than consumed. Fishermen of the Ruby Sea avail themselves of its poison's paralytic properties to more easily catch schools in a single swoop.
36551.name: Ruby-spotted Crab

36552.text: A variety of corpse-eater that has found an icy home in the deep, dark depths of the Ruby Sea, this scavenger sustains itself with the marrow of skeletons and other carrion that drifts down to its watery lair.
36552.name: Marrow-eater

36553.text: A long, smooth-looking wavekin that seemingly snakes across the seafloor, preying upon the smaller creatures that call those same reefs home. Those tempted to pet it should note that save for its coloration and fluid movements, it is not remotely feline.
36553.name: Cloudy Cat Shark

36554.text: These wavekin are capable of gliding effortlessly through the waters thanks to their winglike pectoral fins and sizable air bladders─the latter of which occasionally produces a distasteful trumpeting noise.
36554.name: Red Gurnard

36555.text: A variety of albino sea pickle exclusively found in the Ruby Sea. Those in possession of one are said to be so blessed with incredible fortune that a merchant from Kugane once offered as much as Isari earns in a year to get their hands on this wavekin─a deal which the village gladly accepted.
36555.name: Dream Pickle

36556.text: These wavekin's scales shine with an uncommon luster akin to blood red snow on a sunny day. Known for their unusual migratory habits, they travel even to the One River's more turbulent brackish waters, favoring colder climes.
36556.name: Ruby Haddock

36557.text: This creature's curious coloration has granted it a diadem of azure and gold. As if to support its claim to its crown, it assumes an air of haughty grandeur, which other species of wavekin seem to find off-putting.
36557.name: Crown Fish

36558.text: With its armored scales and beastly fangs, few creatures are fool enough to encroach upon this wavekin's territory. Local legends claim it spawned from the blood of a fisherman who died protecting Isari from piratical pillaging.
36558.name: Sword of Isari

36559.text: Between its colossal size and lustrous lazuline scales, this shark is easily spotted weaving through the reedbeds and inlets of the Ruby Sea, where it migrates after its time spent in more open oceans.
36559.name: Blue Shark

36560.text: The signature mineral barbs lining this wavekin's back were ossified in the scorching heat of the deep waters near Hells' Lid. Its skin is nigh impregnable, and those who attempt to prey upon it are oft left with broken teeth for their efforts.
36560.name: Barb of Exile

36561.text: This wavekin's appearance is redolent of the portly monk who, in the myths of the Far East, represents joy and prosperity. For this reason, the fishing hamlets of the Ruby Sea give this creature pride of place at celebratory meals.
36561.name: Smooth Lumpfish

36562.text: These circular wavekin have a tendency to cluster around the hydrothermal vents near Hells' Lid, thus giving rise to their name. As the waters can reach several hundred degrees, however, their ability to actually cap said Hells is limited by the unfortunate realities of being flesh rather than stone.
36562.name: Hells' Cap

36563.text: This wavekin's chief form of defense is its conspicuous membranous appendage, which it can inflate to ward off potential predators on the hunt for a small, easy meal.
36563.name: Keeled Fugu

36564.text: Though they belong to the seas of the Far East, these fish bear a striking number of similarities to the wahoo found in Eorzean waters. They congregate in small pods, and move with the seasons.
36564.name: Eastern Seerfish

36565.text: This wavekin boasts not only bright, beautiful shades, but a hefty price at market as well. Its eggs can be found dotting the shoals once the ice of winter thaws, making it a welcome harbinger of spring.
36565.name: False Fusilier

36528.text: The prized delicacy of Thavnair's Akyaali, this wavekin is most often served marinated or broiled. It is one of the Near East's chief exports─a testament to its toothsomeness.
36528.name: Akyaali Sardine

36529.text: This invertebrate's signature sanguine hue can be attributed to its reef's calcareous quality and its own predilection for absorption. When it feels threatened, it will feign death by disemboweling itself, excreting its internal organs to befuddle its foes.
36529.name: Spicy Pickle

36530.text: The defining dorsal fin of this wavekin allows it to read aether currents with surprising ease. Come spawning season, it uses this unique ability to locate aether-rich locations where it will lay its eggs.
36530.name: Mayavahana

36531.text: This variety of wavekin is closely related to the bass found in the Far East. Unlike their stoic brethren, however, these fish stubbornly stick to the paradisiacal climes of Thavnair.
36531.name: Hedonfish

36532.text: Hannish legends have it that the satrap's ancestors once rebuffed a dragon of fierce repute, which is no doubt why this serpentine deep-sea wavekin was honored─or placated; it is difficult to tell─with such a name.
36532.name: Satrap Trapfish

36533.text: To stare at this wavekin's cerulean body is to gaze upon the unspoiled waters of the southern seas. Unfortunately, once the creature dies, its lazuline beauty decays to a coal black, rendering its scales unworkable for cosmetic purposes.
36533.name: Blue Marlin

36534.text: A jellyfish that glides through the seas subtly as a susurrus. Its cloud-like form calls to mind the satrap's residence, Meghaduta─and if ever Radz–at–Han's ruler needed a messenger, it would surely make for a stunning one.
36534.name: Satrap's Whisper

36537.text: With its silvery scales and elegant movements, this wavekin invites comparison to the elegant performers that brighten Radz–at–Han's dining establishments. Mirroring its namesakes' popularity, this aquatic dancer can be seen attracting throngs at the bazaar on any given day.
36537.name: Meyhane Reveler

36536.text: A docile wavekin that keeps to the shadows of kelp and rocks. It makes a delicious addition to most any meal, as its every part down to the most unappealing of organs has been found to be a delight for the palate.
36536.name: Shallows Cod

36539.text: A saltwater wavekin capable of living well over fifty years. Little wonder, then, that its name derives from the word for “vitality,” and that those in Thavnair use it to symbolize longevity.
36539.name: Rasa Fish

36538.text: Though it looks as if it might well have been perfected in the alchemists' fires, this wavekin in fact hails from faraway seas. Migration is what brings it to Thavnair, where it adopts the metallic hue for which it is known.
36538.name: Daemir's Alloy

36547.text: Contrary to its terrifying appearance, this sea-dweller is a rather docile creature. That is not to say it is easy prey, however─when threatened, it bears its visibly lethal fangs, and only desperate fishermen looking to exchange flesh for delicious flesh are foolish enough to face it.
36547.name: Dusky Shark

36540.text: According to local legend, this crustacean was born from the handprint left at water's edge by Agama, a sainted ascetic of Thavnair. As such, it is thought to represent the purgation of evil.
36540.name: Agama's Palm

36541.text: A tropical fish boasting a striped tail and bright scarlet scales at its fore. It is said to have once been a monk, nose rouged with drink, who tripped into the Font of Maya and was summarily reincarnated─which, given the number of tetra to be found there, does raise questions about the frequency of such occurrences.
36541.name: Rummy-nosed Tetra

36542.text: With an appearance often likened to that of the stunted blades carried by the guardians of Thavnair's holy places, this fish is easily mistaken for an abandoned weapon floating up from the depths in defiance of nature.
36542.name: Monksblade

36543.text: A fish that likes to travel in schools which, with their bright coloration, resemble ripe amra swaying in the breeze. When spawning, it keeps its eggs stuffed safely in its mouth like so many seeds of the aforementioned fruit.
36543.name: Atamra Cichlid

36544.text: This wavekin's thin, long body pierces Thavnair's waters like the roots of its well-adapted trees. A useful disguise─but not so useful that man has not learned how delicious it tastes when grilled on a skewer above an open flame.
36544.name: Root of Maya

36545.text: This fish boasts unique scale patterns that resemble─and shine unnervingly in the dark like─a thousand eyes, though its name indicates that this is subject to interpretation on the part of the beholder. Growing up to a few yalms in size, it can be found swimming languidly through the Font of Maya.
36545.name: Floral Snakehead

36566.text: These small crabs mimic pebbles scattered around boulders on the sea floor. While the shell is thick and there is little edible flesh, it is an indispensable part of a pirate's diet thanks to its suitability for stock.
36566.name: Skipping Stone

36567.text: This fish sports a body like that of a shrimp, a head that resembles a frog's, and a pattern that one would be forgiven for mistaking for the pox. The Kojin are said to use these critters for divination, believing that everything from the size of the upcoming catch to one's romantic future can be read in the number of spots upon them.
36567.name: Red-spotted Blenny

36571.text: These crimson-scaled fish have exceptionally tall and thin diamond-shaped bodies. The sight of them swimming in a school─a familiar spectacle in which fishermen delight─is oft likened to that of a red mosaic surfing the seas.
36571.name: Deepbody Boarfish

36569.text: From the reaches of the Glass Ocean to the depths of the Ruby Sea, this creature dwells far and wide─and goes by many names. While its white flesh is light, it has a pleasing texture, and its roe is known for its rich flavor.
36569.name: Grey Mullet

36570.text: These creatures are cousins to the striped rays used by the Kojin as mounts. Due to their translucent flesh, seen as testament to their divinity, they are revered as living seats for the most sagacious.
36570.name: Prayer Cushion

36581.text: This creature's defining feature is its tooth-lined jaw, which spirals out and forward in a horrific loop. This exposed lower mandible can never be completely closed, but this is hardly necessary with the level of carnage that simply whipping its head around to saw through its prey creates.
36581.name: Uzumaki

36572.text: In stark contrast to its closest kin, the seahorse, this wavekin has a smooth, tubular body. It is known to swim vertically, an adaptation that naturalists suspect is intended to mimic the movement of seaweed.
36572.name: Jointed Razorfish

36575.text: A fiery wavekin dwelling amongst the coral reefs, its coloration calls to mind the clothing donned by fell spirits, the yasha, traditionally thought to reside on the Isle of Zekki.
36575.name: Mini Yasha

36574.text: A fish with tawny-brown coloring on the side it prefers to show to the world, and pale white where it lies upon the sea floor. Among this species one will find the occasional giant, some spanning up to five yalms in size.
36574.name: Righteye Flounder

36577.text: Bony protrusions line this fish's body and sucker-like fins extend from its abdomen. An inept swimmer, it uses these fins to cling to rocks on the seabed where it spends the majority of its life.
36577.name: Othardian Lumpsucker

36576.text: According to Far Eastern legend, when the kami built the very first shrine, it was this shark's convenient snout that they borrowed to do so. This being the case, it enjoys massive popularity among carpenters as a token of good fortune─fortune that presumably does not extend to the creature itself.
36576.name: Sawshark

36579.text: Always on the prowl for prey, this wavekin devours fish up to its own size and even the hardest of crustaceans. Its beautiful fins are known for their ability to capture aether from the surrounding waters, and shine a deep blue as it cruises the seas.
36579.name: Bluefin Trevally

36582.text: The sacks their kin use for storing poison are adapted by this creature to instead accumulate carbonate minerals from the deposits found on the beds of salt lakes. Gyr Abanians dry this fish to make a dehydrating agent used for interring their dead.
36582.name: Natron Puffer

36583.text: The fins on this wavekin's abdomen allow it to cleave through waters of varying salinity with ease. They can even cut through the waters in the depths of the lochs─where the pressure is extreme─with the swiftness of a thrown dagger.
36583.name: Diamond Dagger

36584.text: Enveloping their thin bodies in an assortment of white crystals, these creatures attempt to mimic the boulders found on salty lochbeds. With said crystals varying from great to small, the wavekin resemble fans adorned with quartz and pearls, such as the rich and boastful might carry.
36584.name: Queenly Fan

36585.text: White with black spots, this serpentine wavekin looks like the typical panther might after its observer has pressed their fists to their eyes for some time─an action that naturalists stress is not recommended.
