While it moves with the speed one would expect of a carnivore, due to its poor eyesight coupled with the near nonexistent light deep below the surface, it is sadly inept at finding prey.
36585.name: Pale Panther

36586.text: A squid that grows to enormous size thanks to the abundance of minerals that amass in the depths of its high-salinity environment. While favored by local Highlanders for its nutritious flesh, most find this loch-dweller too salty for their tastes.
36586.name: Saltsquid

36587.text: With eyes on either side of its protruding head, this predator misses none of what happens deep in the loch. It rules its waters with a fist more iron than platinum, hunting down the prey it sets its bulging eyes upon to the very end.
36587.name: Platinum Hammerhead

36568.text: Small sky blue dots pattern this creature's otherwise monochrome body. While its few larger black markings may be suspected of camouflaging the true location of its eyes, they in fact are a by-product of this fish's aether-sensitive organs, and─rather dangerously─mark said organs' position.
36568.name: Othardian Wrasse

36578.text: With a head shape eerily reminiscent of a samurai's helmet, it is no surprise that warriors once attempted to don this fish's skull as a form of protection. One will also not be shocked to hear that it was far from effective, being easily penetrated by enemy katana.
36578.name: Shogun's Kabuto

36573.text: Inhabiting the coral reef and its neighboring sands, this creature peeks out from its abode to expose the white, arrow-shaped pattern on its head only once in a blue moon. Though it lacks many a spot compared to the garden eels it so resembles, it at least shares their bulging and slightly confused eyes.
36573.name: Pipefish

36546.text: Primordial beings with glimmering teeth so sharp as to earn them the name “blade's ray.” Known to hunt birds in addition to other fish, they propel themselves through the surface with powerful strokes before their prey gets any hint of danger.
36546.name: Xiphactinus

36580.text: A leisurely shark partial to life at the bottom of the seas. While many mistakenly believe it to have skin tougher than armor, this is but a misnomer wrapped in an old wives' tale. Though comparably inflexible for a creature of the deep seas, when brought ashore, its hide is far from what it is cracked up to be.
36580.name: Kitefin Shark

36535.text: A small tropical fish that inhabits the coral reefs off of Tebqeyiq. Males boast bright blue and yellow patterning to court females, which keep to an arguably drab grey-black.
36535.name: Tebqeyiq Smelt

36659.text: Among the cephalopods found in salt lakes, this particular wavekin boasts the largest ink sac despite its diminutive size. Treasured as a delicacy in Gyr Abania, its ink is well known for the abundant minerals contained within it, and its pungent kick is ever a delight to those whose family traditions involve a nice lick of licking salt.
36659.name: Inksquid

36661.text: According to Far Eastern legend, this clam emits light of comparable beauty to that which radiates from the very goddess of auroras herself. A coveted ingredient for mother-of-pearl inlays, some believe that simply adorning tableware with its shell will improve the taste of food, a flimsy theory Sharlayan cuisine has put to the proof time and time again.
36661.name: Auroral Clam

38811.text: Though the waters surrounding the Isle of Ken can sink to frigid temperatures, this freshwater fish thrives by generating copious amounts of body heat. This internal aetheric reaction is far more than simple thermoregulation, however, as the flesh of this creature retains its uncanny heat even after trimmed and gutted.
38811.name: Ken Kiln

38813.text: This bivalve mollusk is of such a clear and delicate color, it perfectly resembles an errant petal plucked from a flower in the blush of spring. Perhaps this is why the pixies were so quick to name it for their forebear Glorianda, in imitation of the Jenanna's tear of Longmirror Lake.
38813.name: Glorianda's Tear

38939.text: This wavekin's mottled green pattern gives it the impression of being clad in weathered bronze─a perception not far from the truth. Its scales, suffused by the mineral waters of Bronze Lake, are known to contain traces of rare metal.
38939.name: Verdigris Guppy

38837.text: Known─and named─for its unique style of swimming, this freshwater fish skips rapidly from rock to rock as it traverses the lake floor. It does this not for the sheer joy of living, but to inflict a swift, unpredictable death upon the smaller wavekin that it hunts for food.
38837.name: Lakeskipper

38838.text: Legend has it that this smooth-scaled eel of dark bronze came into existence only after a lancer hurled a slain comrade's spear into the lake. The story fails to mention whether the lancer was ever aware of this miraculous genesis, or if it sparked a craze of submerging postmortem mementos in large bodies of water.
38838.name: Bronze Eel

38839.text: This member of the peacock bass family is recognizable for its bold stripes, the deep green markings a stunning reflection of the lake's emerald waters. Spearfishers consider this fish one of the region's prize catches.
38839.name: Striped Peacock Bass

38840.text: The scales of this distinctive trout range from a deep olive green to a gleaming bronze brown. Its crimson flesh is highly sought after by fishermen, who equate the darker hue with a richer─and thus more expensive─flavor.
38840.name: Bronze Trout

38841.text: This “unexpected predator,” as naturalists have dubbed it, is a surprisingly harmonious cog in the local ecology. Despite its prehistoric appearance, the massive nosceasaur appears to consciously avoid disrupting the food chain's delicate equilibrium.
38841.name: Nosceasaur

41060.text: An abundant mollusk, the empyreal spiral is the source of many of Saibai Cavern's beautiful shells and, in turn, its name. The shells have long been used in the artisanal works of Sui no Sato─in particular, a pigment that shimmers with rainbow hues.
41060.name: Empyreal Spiral

41062.text: As its name suggests, the opal tetra's scales gleam with brilliant color. Indeed, it is no less precious than a gem to aquarists, who firmly believe that the mere sight of the iridescent wavekin can cure most ails.
41062.name: Opal Tetra

43803.text: Although a variety of loach species are present throughout Tural, this one in particular has by far the most ancient lineage. Fitting, perhaps, that this progenitor should call Karvarhur the First home.
43803.name: Turali Loach

43804.text: After observing the similarity between this creature's large eyes and those of the Yok Huy, one eager Wing of Reflection researcher posited the existence of a shared ancestor. Alas, there proved to be no tangible link, leaving the young naturalist rather deflated.
43804.name: Yok Huy Toad

43805.text: According to Yok Huy legend, this fish first came into being when a fallen shard of stone sprouted fins and flopped into the water. It effortlessly blends in with the rocks littering the lakebed, making it hard for predators to spot.
43805.name: Stone Pleco

43806.text: Records indicate that Urqopacha may once have been part of the ocean, leading some scholars to surmise that this wavekin is a descendant of seafaring sharks. Its pointed dorsal fin and sleek form do much to give credence to the notion.
43806.name: Shark Catfish

43807.text: The array of mottled colors adorning this wavekin are the basis for its name. In the Yok Huy tongue, “Zeh Lar Dor” means “the fish that shines with every color from the depths of the earth to the farthest reaches of the night sky.”
43807.name: Zeh Lar Dor

43808.text: The Yok Huy creation myth speaks of a spirit guide appearing in the form of a giant wavekin. Given its size and ancient lineage, scholars believe this fish may have some connection to the legend.
43808.name: Karvarichthys

43809.text: The black, uniform vertical stripes of this wavekin appear as if daubed on with an ink-laden brush. Each time a specimen with a different number of markings is caught, the debate over whether such variations warrant separate classification is rekindled.
43809.name: Severum

43810.text: To watch a shoal of these floral fish dart among the shimmering reeds is to witness a profusion of color─akin to a spring tree laden with blossoms.
43810.name: Ligaka Blossom

43811.text: Stories tell of a Moblin artisan who, as a jest, finished one of their pots with a rather unsightly glaze. Allegedly, the artless creation gained a mind of its own and transformed into a stingray. Thanks to the fanciful tale, this wavekin has earned itself admirers among earthenware aficionados.
43811.name: Potglaze Stingray

43812.text: When seen weaving through the water, these reddish fish take on the appearance of flames flickering in the depths. Indeed, the legend surrounding this wavekin tells of a torch─jettisoned by a bandit in a bid to shake their pursuers─coming to life underwater.
43812.name: Emberwisp

43813.text: A species of colossoma that bears a striking resemblance to a pipira. It is speculated that this trait is conducive to survival─pipira are not observed to be cannibals. Yet.
43813.name: Ihuyka Colossoma

43814.text: The name of this freshwater fish refers to its fiery orange tail fin. Despite the visual similarity, there seems to be no love lost between this species and the emberwisp.
43814.name: Torchtail

43815.text: Legend has it that these colorful wavekin are descendants of two scaly sisters born from a mighty rainbow. As they dart and weave through the depths, their movements form tiny bridges of iridescent light.
43815.name: Variegated Sisterscale

43816.text: The flesh of this sucker-mouthed fish may lack flavor, but owing to its plentiful numbers─not to mention the ease with which it can be caught─it has come to be an important staple food.
43816.name: Kozama'uka Characin

43817.text: This wavekin's ember-like markings are but one explanation for its name. Thanks to an aetherial gland within its body, this eel is able to generate a modicum of heat─comparable, say, to a smoldering chunk of charcoal.
43817.name: Charcoal Eel

43818.text: Despite its undeniable aesthetic appeal, this species is entirely unsuited for aquariums─primarily due to its penchant for frenzied aggression. When encountering their prey, these wavekin attack en masse, leaving nary a scale behind.
43818.name: Rainbow Pipira

43819.text: Preferring to trawl the silty sediment than roam in open water, this species of catfish can grow to a length of almost three yalms. As it matures, this fish must search ever longer to find a resting nook large enough to accommodate its bulk.
43819.name: Lau Lau

43820.text: When shoals of this colorful fish converge, they almost look like petals of a mysterious flower, blooming majestically underwater. It is said that many have been sent to a watery grave trying to lay their hands on the apparition.
43820.name: Ligaka Pirarucu

43821.text: The black stripe to the rear of this wavekin's body gives the impression of a forked tail, or even a pair of leg-like appendages─prompting wonder or revulsion, depending on the observer. This intriguing illusion has earned the fish a nickname: “the two-legged swimmer.”
43821.name: Piraputanga

43822.text: Said to have once inhabited a vast stretch of Ihuykatumu, this colossal predator is without match in present-day Marsh Ligaka.
43822.name: Purussaurus

43823.text: This crab's carapace is almost indistinguishable from the deep blue waters of the caldera lakes it calls home, lending it an advantage when hunting prey and avoiding predators. Turning bright red when boiled, its shell is soft, tender, and very much edible.
43823.name: Turali Land Crab

43824.text: This wavekin was once the unwitting subject of taboo. Likening its thick, fleshy dorsal fin to a Hoobigo's comb, the Xbr'aal used to revile the fish, reminding them as it did of their bitter conflict with the Mamool Ja.
43824.name: Crested Goby

43825.text: This sizable turtle favors the still depths of water-filled calderas. It is also said to have a unique talent for memorizing waterways, and is occasionally observed moving between lakes linked to one another via channels and subterranean passages.
43825.name: Tsoly Turtle

43826.text: The speed and brutality with which it feeds upon its prey is often likened to the signature fighting style of the viper─not the scalekin, but the skilled hunter by the same name.
43826.name: Viperfish

43827.text: This species of crocodile is endemic to the Ut'ohmu Horizon. While it's not uncommon to spot one sunbathing on the shore, approach at your own peril.
43827.name: Horizon Crocodile

43828.text: The bright green hue comes not from its scales, but the moss with which it cloaks itself. Some have speculated that it does this to better resemble a crocodile and therefore deter predators.
43828.name: Tsoly Gar

43829.text: Each of its scales is embedded with a tiny crystal that reflects the light of the sun. When in danger, it uses the bright, dazzling glint to blind its predators.
43829.name: Sunlit Prism

43830.text: By placing a freshly caught fategazer on a platter, local custom dictates that the future can be divined from the number of times it flops helplessly before falling to the ground.
43830.name: Fategazer

43831.text: In Iq Br'aax, this fish is considered auspicious due to its physical resemblance to the fine drapery worn at festivals. Eating it is said to grant good fortune.
43831.name: Frillfin Goby

43832.text: The black ibruq is generally mild-mannered for its size, but the moment it catches sight of its prey, it will charge forward and ram the poor creature over and over until it stops moving.
43832.name: Black Ibruq

43833.text: This particular variety of peacock bass gains new speckles as it matures. The oldest known specimens are said to have upwards of a hundred or more.
43833.name: Speckled Peacock Bass

43834.text: There are countless tales of intrepid adventurers so desperate for any clue of the golden city that they scour the caldera lakes in search of this elusive golden fish.
43834.name: Golden Characin

43835.text: This black-striped wavekin is drawn to fallen leaves floating on the water's surface. It feeds not upon the leaves themselves, as one may be led to believe, but the hapless insects that fall into the water along with them.
43835.name: Deadleaf Minnow

43836.text: People in olden times would keep these shining creatures as pets, particularly if they could not afford ordinary oil lanterns.
43836.name: Glistening Discus

43837.text: Fishers must exercise caution when aiming their spears at this eel, lest they inadvertently pierce its lightning gland and receive a nasty shock for their trouble.
43837.name: Lightning Eel

43838.text: Locals believe the elongated fins of this Yak T'el native are actually an impressive set of whiskers. Naturalists, however, are quick to point out that these appendages are unmistakably fins, citing numerous taxonomical studies as evidence. Judging by the creature's name, such protestations continue to fall on deaf ears.
43838.name: Longwhisker Lungfish

43839.text: Beloved by many, this wavekin's durable golden scales have been put to different uses over the years, and at one point were even used as a form of currency. Presently, the Xbr'aal utilize the scales to decorate their armor, to splendidly shiny effect.
43839.name: Minted Arowana

43840.text: Equipped with a mouthful of razor-sharp fangs, this wavekin has an impressive, albeit terrifying, dedication to satiating its hunger. Not content to subsist on waterborne prey alone, it will attack and consume any mammal or bird that happens to fall into the water. Some believe these fish to be the resurrected spirits of the equally deadly br'aax.
43840.name: Br'aaxfish

43841.text: Roughly translated, “Iq Rrax” means “fresh blood”─a fitting name for a crustacean that consumes exactly that. Capable of filling its claws with the blood of its prey, it will draw on these grisly reserves during times of scarcity.
43841.name: Iq Rrax Crab

43842.text: This colossal cod bears a passing resemblance to the mounts favored by the Mamool Ja. According to one legend, this species came into being when a fleeing wivre plunged into the water and promptly underwent a remarkable transformation.
43842.name: Wivre Cod

43843.text: This diminutive wavekin possesses a highly efficient aether storage gland. Using the accumulated energy to manipulate the currents around it, the warmouth can propel itself to frightening speeds.
43843.name: Warmouth

43844.text: Favoring still waters, this species moves around by frantically flapping its diminished fins. The Hhetsarro consider this wavekin to be a symbol of diligence and earnest effort.
43844.name: Shaaloani Goby

43845.text: This migratory fish traverses the extensive waterways of Xak Tural in time with the seasons. Some nomadic Hhetsarro revere this wavekin as a spirit guide, following it hither and thither on its unceasing journey.
43845.name: Sauger

43846.text: Found up and down the length of Niikwerepi, this pungent fish is ill-suited for consumption. On the other hand, its vigor and stamina make it a prime target for veteran anglers seeking a worthy challenge.
43846.name: Niikwerepi Bass

43847.text: When dried, the long nose of this predator hardens and shrinks to a sharp point. Scholars have traced the origins of the popular pastime “darts” to a rather more rudimentary game─one which saw contestants hurling the desiccated carcasses of these fish like javelins.
43847.name: Longnose Gar

43848.text: Hiding in the very depths of Lake Toari, or “lake of dawn,” this dark grey wavekin is easily mistaken for a patch of gloom the morning light has somehow forgotten to illuminate.
43848.name: Midnight Carp
